newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S. forces on Guam silent on B-52 report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. forces on Guam silent on B-52 report.

text.p: United States forces on Guam declined comment on Tuesday on reports that B-52 bombers carrying cruise missiles had taken off from the Pacific island.
A spokesman at Anderson Air Force base on Guam said by telephone he could not comment on the CNN reports, which quoted Pentagon sources, "for reasons of operational security".
The spokeman's comment came as indications grew that the United States was preparing to launch a military response to Iraq's attack against Kurds in northern Iraq.
The United States has stationed warships armed with Tomahawk cruise missiles in the Gulf and earlier moved B-52 bombers carrying air-launched cruise missiles to Guam.
The B-52s can fly non-stop into missile range several hundred miles from Iraq.
The United States said Iraqi troops appeared to be moving deeper into Kurdish opposition-held territory in northern Iraq, and that President Bill Clinton had readied a "course of action" in response.
